text: Verdict CONFIRMED on DMPK-01: I re-ran the reviewer's vocabulary grep myself across all four files. Every string they list returns zero: dose, dosing, dosage, route, administ*, intravenous, subcutaneous, intrathecal, intranasal, infusion, bolus, half-life, bioavailab*, exposure, plasma, serum, CSF, cerebrospinal, microdialysis, efflux, P-gp, MDR1, MDCK, BCRP, transcytosis, permeab*, Papp, protease, peptidase, proteolysis, aggregation, solubility, excipient, lyophil, hemolysis, anti-drug, transferrin, TfR, unbound. Word-boundary greps for Kp, fu, Vd, PK and ADA also return exactly 0 in all four files, which closes the substring loophole the reviewer flagged. I confirmed each claimed artifact individually: 'clearance' occurs 6 times and is glutamate/autophagic/lysosomal/phagocytic clearance every time (README.md:89; app.js:64,65,112,333,359); 'vial' occurs 3 times and is the FontAwesome class fa-flask-vial every time (index.html:35,89,117); 'oral' matches only inside querySelectorAll. 'therapeutic' occurs exactly 14 times, as claimed. I read openDrugModal (app.js:596-653) and confirmed the innerHTML block at 606-643 renders exactly six numbered fields -- chemStruct, sequence, bindingSites, targets, affinity, safety -- none pharmacokinetic. index.html:326 reads '25 De Novo Targeted Therapeutics Precision Center' verbatim, and README.md:45 reads 'We engineered 25 targeted bio-conjugate therapeutics'. The reasoning is also correct: the leaderboard (app.js:869-895) ranks on pLDDT, dG and CEI with no exposure term, so the platform's prioritisation is affinity-only. Nothing in this finding is overstated. Correction: None on the facts. Two notes on the proposed fix rather than the finding. (1) Instruction (3) -- 'a predicted Kp,uu,brain with an explicit credible interval' -- directly contradicts DMPK-07's own (correct) instruction to render 'OUT OF DOMAIN' for a 4 kDa hydrophilic polypeptide. Implemented as written, DMPK-01 replaces one set of invented numbers with a newer, better-dressed set. DMPK-07's instruction must govern, and DMPK-01 should be reworded to require route, target compartment and an explicit out-of-domain flag rather than a predicted Kp,uu value. (2) index.html:39 is cited as evidence but reads '25 De Novo Drug Center', not 'Therapeutics'; index.html:326 and README.md:45 carry the claim, and the citation should rest on those.

text: Verdict CONFIRMED_WITH_CORRECTION on DMPK-02: I parsed all 25 sequence fields out of app.js myself and recomputed every descriptor independently (average residue masses, EMBOSS pKa set, Kyte-Doolittle, sliding-window Eisenberg). The reviewer's physicochemistry reproduces almost exactly: length 26-47 (median 35.5 vs their 35); MW 2877-5436 Da (median 4112 vs their 4094); net charge at pH 7.4 spanning -7.20 to +8.93, identical to the digit; pI 3.45-10.95 vs their 3.44-10.95; GRAVY -1.12 to +0.26, median -0.92, identical. Their three spot-checked rows reproduce: X1 at app.js:143 = 47 aa, 5340 Da, GRAVY -0.94 (charge -0.61 vs their -0.54, a trivial pKa-set difference); X2 at app.js:153 = 36 aa, 4943 Da, q +8.93, pI 10.95, GRAVY -1.09, 36.1% Arg+Lys, all exact; X3 at app.js:163 = 28 aa, 3508 Da, q -7.20, pI 3.45, exact. I confirmed no candidate carries an RMT shuttle, Fc, TfR1/CD98hc binder or transporter ligand. I re-derived their dose arithmetic for X2 from scratch: 3xKd = 6.3 nM unbound brain, Kp,uu 0.01, fu 0.05, Vd 0.1 L/kg, t1/2 27 min gives CL 10.8 L/h and 16.1 g/day by continuous infusion, and 0.109 g/day under their generous parameter set -- their 16 g/day and 0.11 g/day are correct, as is the >3-log spread. I verified the Pardridge calibration numbers directly in the Europe PMC full text (PMC10426772): '0.07% ID/Gram' for the murine precursor of bapineuzumab, '0.028% ID/Gram' for mAb158, and 'the level of IgG in primate brain following IV administration is <0.01% of the plasma concentration' all appear verbatim. Pardridge 2020 (PMID 33207605) states verbatim that 98% of small molecules and ~100% of biologics do not cross the BBB and that <1% of AD projects used a BBB delivery technology. The core conclusion stands. Correction: Three corrections. (1) The stated ground truth 'roughly 8-10 hydrogen-bond donors' is wrong. Pajouhesh & Lenz give HBD < 3 and HBA < 7, with total H-bonds < 8.8; the reviewer has conflated the total-H-bond ceiling with the donor ceiling, making the quoted limit roughly threefold too permissive. Correcting it strengthens the finding: on my count (44-90 donors, median 72) the candidates exceed an HBD<3 limit by ~15-30x, not the 5-13x claimed. My donor counts also differ from theirs (they report 52-106, median 80) purely by counting convention; the conclusion is convention-independent. (2) 'Nothing in these 25 designs does better than an IgG at crossing' is an overstatement and is the one sentence in this review a motivated author could rebut. Adsorptive-mediated transcytosis is an established, if crude, BBB route for polycationic peptides and CPPs, with published 6-30x enhancements of conjugated payload brain uptake for SynB and penetratin conjugates. The four candidates at net charge +4.8 to +8.9 with 27-36% Arg+Lys are precisely that chemotype and would be expected to exceed IgG's 0.028-0.07 %ID/g. AMT is low-efficiency, non-saturable, non-selective and carries heavy peripheral and renal uptake, so it does not rescue the designs -- but the claim should be narrowed to 'no candidate carries a specific, saturable receptor-mediated transport mechanism; the only plausible route is non-selective AMT, which is not a delivery strategy'. (3) 'glomerular charge trapping' is backwards: the glomerular basement membrane is anionic, so charge selectivity favours filtration of polycations rather than trapping them. The real renal liability, which the review omits entirely, is proximal-tubule reabsorption and accumulation -- the mechanism behind polymyxin and aminoglycoside nephrotoxicity.

text: Verdict CONFIRMED_WITH_CORRECTION on DMPK-03: I implemented the Eisenberg normalized-consensus hydrophobic moment with a sliding 18-residue, 100-degree window independently and reproduced the candidate values to three decimals: X2/B1 (app.js:153, 247) muH = 0.893 at q +8.93, 36.1% Arg+Lys; M4 (app.js:329) muH = 0.883 at q +6.93, 34.4% Arg+Lys; X5 (app.js:183) muH = 0.883 at q +4.79, 27.3% Arg+Lys. Their maximally amphipathic window for X2/B1, KWWKFLRRFWRRLKKYFE, is the window my scan also selects, and it is textbook pore-forming architecture. Three of their four calibration points reproduce on my identical implementation: melittin 0.550 (they said 0.55), pexiganan/MSI-78 0.746 (0.75), (KLAKLAK)2 0.690 (0.69), polyalanine 0.000 (0.00). I confirmed via grep that hemolysis, HC50, MRGPRX2 and complement appear zero times in the codebase, that no infusion-reaction statement exists, and that README.md:99 states verbatim that 'Hydrophobic peptide linkers sterically prevent binding to hERG pore Tyr652/Phe656 residues' for all 25 candidates. Wieprecht 1997 (PMID 9166783) supports the mechanistic rebuttal precisely: the abstract states the analogues were designed with 'retained hydrophobic moment, peptide charge, and angle subtended by the hydrophilic helix region', that PC-rich (mammalian) permeabilisation 'increases drastically with enhanced peptide hydrophobicity', and that 'the antibacterial and hemolytic activity of the peptides increases with enhanced hydrophobicity' with 'a strong correlation ... between the hemolytic effect and the bilayer-permeabilizing activity against PC-rich vesicles'. Maturana 2017 (PMID 28236791) likewise confirms P6 (no antimicrobial, high hemolytic) had 'the highest affinity toward erythrocyte membranes'. The chemotype identification and the safety-gap conclusion are correct. Their proposed flag threshold works: muH > 0.5 and net charge > +3 catches exactly ids 2, 5, 11 and 19 on my numbers and nothing else. Correction: Two corrections, one of which matters. (1) The LL-37 calibration does not reproduce. On the identical Eisenberg scale and identical 18-residue window, full-length LL-37 (LLGDFFRKSKEKIGKEFKRIVQRIKDFLRNLVPRTES) gives muH = 0.894 -- equal to, marginally above, X2/B1's 0.893, not the 0.78 the reviewer reports. The reviewer writes 'LL-37 core', i.e. an unspecified fragment, so the comparison is not reproducible from the stated method. The headline claim 'exceeds LL-37' must be withdrawn and replaced with 'matches LL-37, the best-characterised human membranolytic peptide, and exceeds melittin, pexiganan and (KLAKLAK)2'. That is still a damning statement and is defensible; 'exceeds LL-37' is not. Their 'idealized Leu/Lys amphipathic helix 0.63' is likewise unreproducible -- my LKKLLKLLKKLLKLLKKLLKLL gives 0.807, and an idealised amphipath should sit near the theoretical maximum, so 0.63 suggests a different, unstated sequence. Any calibration table published in this report must ship the exact reference sequences. (2) The quoted safety string is mis-anchored. 'hERG IC50 > 50 uM (0% Cardiotoxicity)' appears only at app.js:147, which is HippoTrk-Saponin-X1 -- not one of the four flagged candidates. The four flagged records say only 'hERG IC50 > 50 uM' (app.js:157, 251, 333) plus 'Tolerance Rate: 0.0%' and 'Peripheral Side Effects: None', which I verified verbatim. The blanket '0% Risk' claim covering all 25 is at README.md:99. Re-anchor the quotation there. Separately, the review would be stronger if it acknowledged that this architecture may be a deliberate CPP/AMT motif rather than an accident -- the finding is that a known dose-limiting liability of the chemotype is unassessed, not that the designers blundered.

text: Verdict CONFIRMED on DMPK-04: I verified the residue mapping myself rather than trusting it. Against canonical Abeta42 (DAEFRHDSGYEVHHQKLVFFAEDVGSNKGAIIGLMVGGVVIA), the string KLVFFAEDVGSNKGAIIGLM is an exact contiguous match to residues 16-35, beginning at Lys16 and ending at Met35; KLVFF maps to Abeta 16-20 and GAIIGLM to Abeta 29-35, exactly as claimed. In APP770/UniProt P05067 numbering, with Abeta1 = APP672, this is residues 687-706 -- the reviewer's range is correct to the residue. I confirmed the fragment is the literal prefix of the candidate-14 sequence at app.js:277 and is contained in the AF3 rank-5 fasta at app.js:129. I independently computed GRAVY for all 25 and confirmed candidate 14 is the sole positive value at +0.26, with every other candidate negative -- the uniqueness claim is exactly right. 'Fibril Blockade: 100%' at app.js:281 and 'Salvianolic Acid B + Abeta Disruptor (KLVFFAED)' at README.md:77 are verbatim, as is the basal-forebrain target string at app.js:279. Greps confirm zero occurrences of aggregation, solubility, thioflavin, seeding, ARIA or oligomer-content anywhere. The pharmacological argument is correct and is the standard position in the field: KLVFF is the self-recognition element of Abeta self-assembly, and beta-sheet-breaker designs deliberately truncate to the minimal motif and abolish self-assembly competence by N-methylation, D-substitution or proline insertion; extending to residue 35 restores the full nucleating unit rather than blocking it. Correction: Two small ones, neither affecting the verdict. (1) The reviewer says the other 24 candidates fall 'between -0.30 and -1.12'; the actual range is -0.34 to -1.12. (2) Calling GRAVY +0.26 'the computational signature of its aggregation propensity' overreaches -- GRAVY is a crude bulk hydropathy average and is not an aggregation predictor. The evidence that carries this finding is the verbatim identity of the amyloidogenic core, which is sufficient on its own; the GRAVY value should be presented as corroborating context, not as a signature. The recommendation to add a TANGO/AGGRESCAN/Waltz-style predictor in the fix is the right instrument for that job.

text: Verdict CONFIRMED_WITH_CORRECTION on DMPK-05: I extracted all 25 sequence fields programmatically and confirmed exactly four byte-identical pairs, at exactly the lines cited: 153/247 (36-mer KWWKFLRRFWRRLKKYFEELWKKLAEKYFELLKKYG), 173/371 (31-mer CKCHGMSGSCSTKTCWWGBLCPFRRACPDCH), 195/319 (41-mer SEAEFRLFRDVWANYCACYPGWLGCDERACPRCHGFWREVC), 205/361 (37-mer VRACPTGKCEGLRGYTCRCEPGWKGPDCRERACPDCH). Distinct-sequence count is 21, as claimed. Every conflicting metadata pair checks out: Kd 2.1 vs 0.65 nM and pLDDT 94.8 vs 94.3 for the same 36-mer, sent to hippocampal CA1 cholinergic terminals and to the nucleus basalis of Meynert respectively; Kd 1.2 vs 2.8 nM (FZD8 agonist in DG SGZ vs ZO-1 protector at BBB endothelium); Kd 1.8 vs 3.8 nM (alpha7 nAChR PAM in PFC vs TLR4/MD-2 antagonist on microglia); Kd 0.85 vs 3.6 nM (TrkB ERK enhancer vs astrocytic EAAT2 upregulator). I also confirmed the reviewer's substantive point about mechanism: no candidate carries a cell-type-restricted ligand, capsid, promoter or locally activated prodrug, and the distribution argument for a freely diffusing peptide in brain ISF is correct. The cited literature is real and says what is claimed -- Huang 2024 (PMID 38753766) states verbatim '40 to 50 times greater reporter expression in the CNS of human [TfR1] knockin mice' and that 'the enhanced tropism was CNS-specific and absent in wild-type mice'; Rezai 2024 (PMID 38169490) states the Abeta reduction 'was numerically greater in regions treated with focused ultrasound than in the homologous regions in the contralateral hemisphere'. Correction: The conclusion is right but the central argument is wrong and must be replaced before this ships. The reviewer writes that a different pLDDT for the same input string 'is not possible for a deterministic model'. That is false twice. First, AlphaFold3 is not deterministic: its structure module is a seeded diffusion model, multiple samples are drawn per seed, and AlphaFold Server returns an ensemble, so identical input legitimately yields different pLDDT across runs. An author could rebut the finding on exactly this point. Second, and decisively, none of these numbers came from AlphaFold at all. app.js:791 computes the displayed pLDDT as `93 + Math.sin(i*0.4)*4 + (char.charCodeAt(0) % 5) * 0.5` and app.js:850 computes PAE as `Math.abs(i-j)*0.4 + (charCodeAt(i%len) % 4)*0.3` -- closed-form functions of residue index and ASCII code, bounded to roughly 89-99 for any input whatsoever. The correct argument is therefore not 'the model is deterministic so the numbers conflict' but 'no pLDDT anywhere in this platform is an AlphaFold output, so all of them, conflicting or not, are fabricated'. Also: the same 36-mer carries a third, different value (92.8) as AF3 candidate CogAChE-PAS-02 at app.js:131, which the reviewer missed and which makes the point unanswerable. Finally, a citation error: 'conflicting metadata at app.js:145/146' should read 155/156 -- lines 145/146 belong to HippoTrk-Saponin-X1, an unrelated record. And 'at most 21 distinct sequences' should note that one of the 21 (app.js:381) is not a sequence at all, leaving 20 real peptides.

text: Verdict CONFIRMED on DMPK-06: This is the most rigorously supported finding in the review and it holds under direct replication. I retrieved the Cavaco 2021 full text from Europe PMC (PMC8301568) and the regression appears verbatim: 'ln t1/2 = 2.226 + 0.053 x NP residues % - 1.515 x W[0,1] + 1.290 x Y[0,1] - 1.052 x pI[0,1]', with NP = presence of nonpolar residues (%), W = absence/presence of at least one Trp, Y = presence of just one Tyr (0) or at least two Tyr (1), pI = pI less than 10 (0) or greater than 10 (1). The validation library range is also verbatim: 'The ln[t1/2] of the 16 peptides in human serum ranged from 2 to 6 (i.e., 7.4 to 403.4 min)'. I then implemented the model myself and applied it to all 24 letter-parseable sequences (mapping B to Asn, as the reviewer evidently did to reach n=24) with nonpolar = AVLIPFMWG. My output matches theirs to the digit: 22 of 24 contain Trp; minimum 7.9 min for HippoDual-TrkB-AMPK-X5 (they said 8); maximum 99.7 min for AstroSuper-CBF-EAAT2-A5 (they said 100); median 26.4 min (they said 26); 18 of 24 below 60 min; 24 of 24 below 120 min. I independently confirmed that no sequence carries cyclisation, D-residue, N-methyl, PEG, lipid, albumin-binder or Fc notation, that the chemStruct fields describe only warhead attachment chemistry, and that README.md:102 states 'Tolerance Downregulation < 4.2% after 30 days' and app.js:157 states 'Tolerance Rate: 0.0%'. The 30-day-pharmacology-versus-minutes-scale-residence contradiction is real. Lau & Dunn (PMID 28720325) confirms '>60 peptide drugs are approved' and 'over 150 peptides in active development'. Correction: Two refinements. (1) The predicted half-lives are more sensitive to an undefined term than the review admits. Cavaco does not fix the membership of 'nonpolar residues'; with AVLIPFMWG I reproduce median 26 min, but including Cys gives median 43 min and excluding Gly and Trp gives median 8 min. The point estimate should be published as a set-dependent range, which is what the reviewer's own fix demands elsewhere and should demand here. (2) The pI term is pI > 10, not pI >= 10 as written; immaterial for these sequences. Substantively I would add that the proteolysis estimate is an upper bound, not the answer, because renal filtration is the parallel clearance pathway the review never quantifies -- see my missed-issues list.

text: Verdict CONFIRMED on DMPK-07: I recomputed the thermodynamic consistency for all 25 records rather than the reviewer's five. At 298 K with RT = 0.5921 kcal/mol, dG = -18.4 kcal/mol implies Kd = 3.195e-5 nM against the stated 0.32 nM, a factor of 10,014 -- the reviewer's 3.2e-5 nM and ~9,900x are correct. Across all 25 records the discrepancy runs from 676x (app.js:384) to 16,046x (app.js:290), bracketing the reviewer's spot-checked 670x-15,800x, and in every single case the stated Kd is weaker than the stated dG implies. That unidirectional bias is itself strong evidence the two numbers were assigned independently rather than derived, exactly as the reviewer infers. Word-boundary greps confirm zero occurrences of Kp, fu, unbound, MDCK, MDR1, P-gp, efflux and Papp in all four files. I read renderLeaderboardTable (app.js:869-895) and renderBenchmarkChart (app.js:1049-1103) and confirmed the ranking columns are pLDDT, dG and CEI only, with the chart plotting CEI against |dG| at app.js:1053-1055. 'Cognitive Enhancement Index' is indeed never defined anywhere in the codebase -- it appears only as a data field (app.js:124-135), a chart label (app.js:1063) and a table header (index.html:306). Loryan 2022 (PMID 35411506) supports the ground truth verbatim: 'the majority of the companies (93%) has established a common understanding across disciplines of the concept and utility of K[p,uu]', '79% of all responders describe the portfolio impact of K[p,uu] implementation in their companies as game-changing', and '74% consider the current toolbox ... satisfactory'. Correction: None on the facts; one on grading. I would raise this from MAJOR to CRITICAL. The dG/Kd inconsistency is presented as a secondary point inside a methodology finding, but it is not a methodological preference -- it is arithmetic proof that the two headline numbers on every one of the 25 cards and the leaderboard were fabricated independently of each other. That is the same class of evidence, and the same degree of certainty, as the duplicate-sequence finding graded CRITICAL at DMPK-05, and it covers 25 records rather than 8. It should either be split into its own CRITICAL fabricated-data finding alongside DMPK-05 or this finding should be regraded. One caution on the fix: 'replace the affinity-only ranking with a composite that requires an exposure term' cannot be implemented honestly on these molecules, because the same finding correctly concludes the exposure predictors are out of domain for 3-5 kDa polypeptides. The implementable instruction is to remove the ranking entirely rather than to reweight it.

text: Verdict CONFIRMED_WITH_CORRECTION on DMPK-08: The three headline defects are real and I verified each. app.js:381 literally sets sequence to 'His14-Phe174-Linker-Peptide-Conjugate'; I traced it through openDrugModal (app.js:600, 648-652) and confirmed all three renderers execute on it unconditionally without crashing, and that copyModalFasta (app.js:660-671) will place that English phrase on the clipboard. The letter B appears at app.js:173, app.js:371 and app.js:130, and I confirmed independently that AlphaFold Server accepts only the 20 standard single-letter codes and rejects B, J, O, U and X -- so the Copy-FASTA-and-launch workflow genuinely emits input the server will refuse for those records. On cysteines, I counted them programmatically: 7 Cys in the 31-mer at app.js:173/371 (correct), 7 Cys in the 37-mer at app.js:205/361 (correct), 8 in the 47-mer at app.js:143 and 8 in the 45-mer at app.js:215 (correct). Greps confirm no disulfide connectivity is specified anywhere, and no oxidative folding, scrambling or thiol-mediated dimerisation discussion exists. The 'Immunogenicity: Low/Very Low' strings are at app.js:167, 271 and 303 exactly as cited. The free-thiol developability argument is sound and standard. Correction: The cysteine census is wrong and must be fixed before publication, because a reviewer who miscounts the thing they are counting loses the room. The actual number of records with an odd cysteine count is 10, not 11, and the id list given (3,4,7,9,12,13,15,16,17,20,22,23) is wrong on four entries: id 3 has 2 Cys (even), id 12 has 6 (even), id 17 has 4 (even), and id 21 -- 5 Cys in a 34-mer at app.js:351 -- is odd and was omitted. The correct set is ids 4, 7, 9, 13, 15, 16, 20, 21, 22, 23 (app.js lines 173, 205, 225, 267, 287, 299, 339, 351, 361, 371). The two 8-Cys records cited as evidence (ids 1 and 8) have even counts and belong to the separate 'high cysteine density' argument, not the free-thiol argument; the reviewer merged the two under the phrase 'odd or high counts', which is what produced the error. Second, the illustrative pLDDT axis labels are wrong: the reviewer writes 'H1 i2 s3 -4 15 44', the actual output is H1, i2, s3, 14, 45, -6, P7, h8. Substance unaffected but do not print a wrong quotation. Third, one defect the reviewer missed in this same finding: copyModalFasta writes the bare sequence with no '>' header (app.js:662), so the button labelled 'Copy FASTA Sequence' never produces FASTA for any of the 25 records, not just the broken one.

rationale: The three headline defects are real and I verified each. app.js:381 literally sets sequence to 'His14-Phe174-Linker-Peptide-Conjugate'; I traced it through openDrugModal (app.js:600, 648-652) and confirmed all three renderers execute on it unconditionally without crashing, and that copyModalFasta (app.js:660-671) will place that English phrase on the clipboard. The letter B appears at app.js:173, app.js:371 and app.js:130, and I confirmed independently that AlphaFold Server accepts only the 20 standard single-letter codes and rejects B, J, O, U and X -- so the Copy-FASTA-and-launch workflow ge

tags: DMPK / CNS drug delivery (neuropharmacokinetics, peptide and biologic developability)
text: Missed by the primary reviewer: THE CENTRAL FABRICATION IS NEVER NAMED. The reviewer treats pLDDT and PAE as though they were real AlphaFold outputs (DMPK-05 argues about determinism; DMPK-07 lists pLDDT as a ranking input). They are not outputs at all. app.js:791 computes every displayed pLDDT as `93 + Math.sin(i*0.4)*4 + (char.charCodeAt(0) % 5) * 0.5`, which returns 89-99 for literally any input string including 'His14-Phe174-Linker-Peptide-Conjugate' (I checked: 89.1-99.0). app.js:850 computes every PAE cell as `Math.abs(i-j)*0.4 + (charCodeAt % 4)*0.3`, a trivial diagonal ramp with no structural content. app.js:674-773 builds the 3D 'backbone' as a Catmull-Rom tube through a helix whose radius is `6 + (charCode % 5) * 0.8` -- geometry from ASCII arithmetic, not coordinates. Against this, app.js:707 comments 'REAL FASTA SEQUENCE PARSING & 3D BACKBONE TOPOLOGY GENERATION', index.html:371 titles the panel 'AlphaFold3 Real Sequence-Driven 3D Model & PAE Heatmap Graphs', index.html:377 labels the viewer 'Real Sequence 3D Structure (pLDDT Color Spectrum)', and README.md:108-110 describes 'Real sequence-driven backbone topology parsing' and 'residue-by-residue confidence profile'. No AlphaFold prediction exists anywhere in this repository. This is the single most serious integrity finding available and the review omits it, which also leaves DMPK-05's argument resting on the refutable claim that AF3 is deterministic.

source.ref: DMPK / CNS drug delivery (neuropharmacokinetics, peptide and biologic developability)

tags: DMPK / CNS drug delivery (neuropharmacokinetics, peptide and biologic developability)
text: Missed by the primary reviewer: THE SECOND BARRIER -- THE PLASMA MEMBRANE -- IS NEVER MENTIONED. The review is entirely about the BBB and stops there. Roughly a third of the 25 candidates name targets that are intracellular, so even a molecule that crossed the BBB perfectly would still be in the wrong compartment: Keap1 Kelch domain (app.js:164, 310, 340), AMPK alpha-subunit kinase domain (app.js:184), GSK-3beta ATP pocket (app.js:226), LC3-II on the autophagosomal membrane (app.js:330), and ER-beta ligand-binding domain (app.js:352, 392). A 3-5 kDa hydrophilic, largely anionic polypeptide cannot reach the cytosol or nucleus; it requires uptake plus endosomal escape, which is the harder of the two delivery problems and for which none of the proposed fixes (TfR1 RMT, CD98hc, intrathecal, FUS, AAV for a peptide payload) provides a solution. Omitting this understates the delivery gap by one entire barrier and makes the recommended remediation look more achievable than it is.

source.ref: DMPK / CNS drug delivery (neuropharmacokinetics, peptide and biologic developability)

tags: DMPK / CNS drug delivery (neuropharmacokinetics, peptide and biologic developability)
text: Missed by the primary reviewer: RENAL CLEARANCE IS ABSENT, WHICH MAKES THE HALF-LIFE ESTIMATE AN UPPER BOUND. Every candidate is 2877-5436 Da, an order of magnitude below the glomerular sieving threshold, so filtration alone drives clearance toward GFR and caps plasma half-life at minutes regardless of proteolysis. The Cavaco proteolytic prediction in DMPK-06 is therefore a ceiling, not an estimate, and the true dose requirement in DMPK-02 and DMPK-06 is understated. Separately, and more importantly for safety: cationic peptides are reabsorbed and accumulate in the proximal tubule, which is the established nephrotoxicity mechanism for polymyxins and aminoglycosides. For the four candidates at net charge +4.8 to +8.9 that would be dosed at gram-per-day scale, renal tubular injury is at least as probable a dose-limiting toxicity as the hemolysis the review does flag, and the kidney appears nowhere in the report.

source.ref: DMPK / CNS drug delivery (neuropharmacokinetics, peptide and biologic developability)

tags: DMPK / CNS drug delivery (neuropharmacokinetics, peptide and biologic developability)
text: Missed by the primary reviewer: THE MOLECULE ANALYSED IS NOT THE MOLECULE CLAIMED. Every record is described as a bio-conjugate, and the chemStruct fields specify large natural-product warheads: ginsenoside Rg1 C42H72O14 (app.js:142), ginsenoside Rb1 C54H92O23 (app.js:204, 360), salvianolic acid B C36H30O16 (app.js:276, 350), curcumin C21H20O6 (app.js:162, 298). The reviewer computed MW, GRAVY, net charge, hydrogen-bond donors and hydrophobic moment for the peptide alone and reported them as the candidate's properties. An Rb1 conjugate adds roughly 930 Da and about eleven further hydrogen-bond donors; salvianolic acid B adds a polyanionic tetracatechol. These warheads are themselves textbook poor CNS penetrants. The physicochemical table needs an explicit caveat that it describes the peptide moiety only and that the actual claimed entity is larger, more polar and worse.

source.ref: DMPK / CNS drug delivery (neuropharmacokinetics, peptide and biologic developability)

tags: DMPK / CNS drug delivery (neuropharmacokinetics, peptide and biologic developability)
text: Missed by the primary reviewer: THE RECOMMENDED FIXES ARE PRESCRIBED WITHOUT THEIR OWN LIMITATIONS. (a) Intrathecal/ICV is offered four times as an alternative route, but CSF-administered macromolecules penetrate brain parenchyma only on the order of hundreds of microns to a couple of millimetres from ependymal and pial surfaces, and human CSF turns over several times per day. IT/ICV will not deliver a 4 kDa peptide to hippocampal CA1 or the nucleus basalis of Meynert -- precisely the deep structures this platform targets -- so as written the recommendation sends the author down a route that fails for the stated indications. (b) TfR1 RMT is prescribed across four findings, with its liabilities relegated to a single clause in a literature note. High-affinity or bivalent TfR engagement causes reticulocyte depletion and acute clinical-chemistry changes; monovalency, affinity tuning and effector-function silencing are prerequisites of the format, not implementation details. A fix reading 'attach a TfR1 shuttle' can reproduce a known safety failure.

source.ref: DMPK / CNS drug delivery (neuropharmacokinetics, peptide and biologic developability)

tags: DMPK / CNS drug delivery (neuropharmacokinetics, peptide and biologic developability)
text: Missed by the primary reviewer: FABRICATED EFFICACY NUMBERS GET A PASS WHILE FABRICATED SAFETY NUMBERS ARE ATTACKED. The review demands 'NOT ASSESSED' for all 25 safety strings but leaves the equally unsupported efficacy point estimates in the same records untouched: 'LTP +280%' (README.md:60, app.js:148), 'dendritic spine density +310%' (README.md:64, app.js:188), 'synaptic ACh +350%' (README.md:74, app.js:252), 'lysosomal degradation +420%' (app.js:333-334), 'CBF +45%' (app.js:355-356), 'working memory span +240%' (app.js:200), 'information processing speed 2x' (README.md:71). These carry no model, no n, no dose and no error bar, and they are the numbers a reader will actually act on. Correcting only one side of the ledger is an asymmetry an author can exploit.

source.ref: DMPK / CNS drug delivery (neuropharmacokinetics, peptide and biologic developability)

tags: DMPK / CNS drug delivery (neuropharmacokinetics, peptide and biologic developability)
text: Missed by the primary reviewer: TWO OF THE SCORED METRICS DO NOT EXIST AS ENDPOINTS. The review treats 'Seizure Index: 0.01-0.02 / 1.0' as an unassessed value that should be relabelled. There is no such normalised in-silico endpoint; like 'Cognitive Enhancement Index' (which the review does correctly flag), it is an invented scale. The same applies to 'Safety Plasticity Score: 99.5 / 100' (app.js:291) and 'Safety Index: 99.1 / 100' (app.js:343). Inventing a metric and then scoring against it is a distinct and more serious defect than failing to measure a real one, and these strings should be deleted rather than populated with 'NOT ASSESSED', which would imply the endpoint is real and merely unrun.

source.ref: DMPK / CNS drug delivery (neuropharmacokinetics, peptide and biologic developability)

tags: DMPK / CNS drug delivery (neuropharmacokinetics, peptide and biologic developability)
text: Missed by the primary reviewer: NO VALIDATION IS DEMANDED OF THE PREDICTORS THE FIXES WOULD INSTALL. The review prescribes a substantial new in-silico DMPK layer -- Kp,uu,brain, fu,plasma, fu,brain, MDCK-MDR1 efflux ratio, Papp, aggregation propensity, serum t1/2 -- but never requires the platform to demonstrate that any of it recovers known answers. The minimum standard before any of these numbers is displayed is a positive-control set: run several marketed CNS small molecules and at least one marketed peptide with published Kp,uu and human t1/2 through the identical pipeline and show the predictions bracket the measured values, with the out-of-domain flag firing on the peptide. Without that, the remediation risks replacing a visibly fabricated dataset with an invisibly fabricated one, which is worse.
